modules.name: auth
modules.description: Registration, login, profile lookup, and a no-op logout. Owns a redundant in-memory cache (_user_cache) of usernames to plaintext passwords, layered on top of a users table that already persists the same data.

modules.name: notes
modules.description: CRUD for user notes against a sqlite notes table. Reaches directly into auth's _user_cache to gate note creation instead of using any interface. Three of its four queries build SQL via string formatting.

modules.name: billing
modules.description: Invoice creation, lookup, listing, and payment against a sqlite invoices table. Parameterizes all queries correctly (unlike notes), but keeps an unbounded, never-expired INVOICE_CACHE that can drift from the database, and has two bare except blocks that silently swallow errors.

modules.name: shared
modules.description: Not a domain module — infrastructure. Flask app factory (create_app) and the sqlite connection helper (get_db/init_db) every other module depends on. Also where the hardcoded SECRET_KEY lives.

entry_points.description: POST /register — creates a user row and warms _user_cache.
POST /login — checks cache first, falls back to a DB read, warms cache on a DB-verified hit.
GET /users/<username> — profile lookup, cache-first, DB fallback.
POST /logout — no session state exists anywhere, so this is a no-op kept for an unspecified frontend caller.
POST /notes — create, gated on auth's cache, string-formatted INSERT.
DELETE /notes/<int:note_id> — the one parameterized query in this module.
POST /billing/invoices — create, parameterized, bare except on payload parsing.
GET /billing/invoices/<int:id> — cache-first read, falls back to DB and repopulates cache.
POST /billing/invoices/<int:id>/pay — bare except around the DB write; cache is mutated to 'paid' even when that except fires, so cache and DB can disagree.

coupling_notes.description: notes/routes.py imports _user_cache directly from auth.routes instead of going through any interface. A note can only be created for a user currently warm in that in-process cache, not any user who exists in the users table.
coupling_notes.evidence: legacy-app/notes/routes.py:8 `from auth.routes import _user_cache`; used as a gate at legacy-app/notes/routes.py:19.

coupling_notes.description: Schema-level coupling via a real foreign key, not just an import — notes.username references users.username, so notes cannot be understood or migrated independently of auth's user table.
coupling_notes.evidence: legacy-app/shared/db.py notes table definition: `username TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(username)`.

coupling_notes.description: Same pattern as notes: invoices.username references users.username.
coupling_notes.evidence: legacy-app/shared/db.py invoices table definition: `username TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(username)`.

deep_dive_notes: Churn is uninformative right now: the whole tree was introduced in a single bootstrap commit, so every module shows churn_commits=1. This will only become a meaningful risk signal once real change history accumulates.

auth stores the same fact (a user's password) in two places that can disagree: the users table and the in-process _user_cache dict. Nothing invalidates the cache when the table changes through another process, and nothing repopulates it on process restart until the next login.

SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in legacy-app/shared/__init__.py ('dev-secret-do-not-use-in-prod-...') and identical across every environment by construction — flagging the existence and location of this secret, not restating its value here.
notes/routes.py builds SQL via Python string formatting (%) in 3 of its 4 routes (create, list, update) — classic injection surface. Only delete_note uses a parameterized query.
billing/routes.py parameterizes every query but has two bare `except:` blocks (create_invoice's payload parsing, pay_invoice's DB write) that swallow all exception types with no logging.
No tests exist anywhere in the target (tests/ is empty). No input validation on any route. No structured logging anywhere in the target.

shared/__init__.py is the one place all three domain modules are wired together (create_app registers all three blueprints) — it's small (69 lines) but structurally central; any change to the app factory or DB helper has blast radius across all three modules.
